chunks: He said: 'Even if I bring you [something] more guided than that which you found your fathers upon?' They said: 'We are disbelievers in what you have been sent with.'

key_terms.کَافِرُونَ: disbelievers / those who cover the truth

ai.seo_question: Who spoke these words in the Quran and what was the people's response?
ai.summary: In Shia tafsir, this verse is often interpreted as a rhetorical challenge by Prophet Jesus (peace be upon him) to his contemporaries, highlighting the stubbornness of those who cling to ancestral tradition (taqlid) over rational evidence. Their declaration of disbelief underscores a recurring Quranic theme: the rejection of divine messengers not due to lack of proof, but due to entrenched pride and adherence to the ways of the forefathers. This dialogue serves as a critique of blind imitation, a key concept in Shia epistemology.
